Name: Christmas_Santa
$Comment: Santa's conversation, everything he says while Christmas runs, wherever his placement stands him (the
Forgotten Temple, unless a server owner moves him). He contracts everything: I'm, you'll, they're.
HOW A SCREEN IS PICKED. Start is walked in a fixed order: First (top to bottom), then a quest that is
READY to hand in, then one he can OFFER, then one that is ACTIVE, then Then, then Fallback.
First holds three things. The off-season line comes first and shows only while Christmas is off (a
visit after a command ends it, or a server owner who stands him somewhere all year), and its only
answer is goodbye. Then his first words, for a player he has not met: what happened to his sleigh,
what to do about it and where, in a few plain lines, kept until the player answers. Then his daily
word, once a day (Once with Period Daily, turning over at midnight UTC), which pays a little favor on
his Nice List when the player finishes the line, whichever way they leave it. Fallback is the menu.
THE SEASON. A conversation has no Season leaf, so the off-season beat and the option that opens the
stall read the feature ziggfreedcommon:feature Christmas_Live, Min 1: while Christmas is off the stall
is not offered, and nobody is sent to a screen that opens closed.
THE HELPERS. Where are your helpers? answers for the whole season in one line: Tomas and Elsie stand
beside Santa, and while Harvest Feast's last days still run (they overlap the start of Christmas)
they are at their feast spots by the kweebec village instead. A conversation gates a line only on its
own season's switch, so the line names both places rather than asking which season runs.
THE FOOTER. Most screens pull in the santa_footer group: the stall, How am I doing on the list? (it
opens the Reputation page, and shows once the player has any favor with him), three lore lines and
goodbye. More of Christmas (quests, the board) joins this conversation as rows and lines of its own.
No line asks which world the player is in, so every line plays wherever he stands. The greeting's
memory carries no Where, so it is kept once per player, the same in every world.
